profile: I’m Valerio, a Cloud Developer working on Google Cloud, with an approach centred on requirements analysis and dialogue with the client. I develop mainly in Python, adopting other languages when the project requires it.

In 2025 I graduated with honours from the University of Bologna, with an MSc in Computer Science and Engineering. My thesis, dedicated to fairness in machine learning, had a concrete outcome: the library I worked on was used in the European AEQUITAS project. Cloud architecture and artificial intelligence remain the two areas I’m most curious about, and that I continue to study.
Outside work, I divide my time between cooking, video games and collecting, without forgetting physical activity and friends.

details: I design and develop solutions on Google Cloud for clients, from gathering requirements to evaluating POCs and architecture choices.
I develop services for serverless applications, data processing and cloud integrations, with Python and FastAPI as my main tools.
I also contribute to CI/CD, IAM, monitoring, logging, troubleshooting and technical support.

I delivered four courses to very different groups: basic Excel for school staff, LEGO Mindstorms robotics for a middle school class, and Snap! programming for two primary school classes. It taught me to explain technology to people starting from zero.
I developed the Angular frontend of an Industry 4.0 data visualisation dashboard, working in an Agile team with Git and CI/CD.

projects.name: FairLib
projects.description: For my MSc thesis I worked on a Python library that helps reduce bias in machine learning models, using fairness techniques in pre-processing and in-processing. My contribution was integrating and improving the existing implementation.
projects.note: The library was used in the European AEQUITAS project, and my name appears among the contributors of one of the project’s research datasets on Zenodo.

projects.name: PositionPal
projects.description: In a group project, I took care of the microservice that handles user registration and profiles: hexagonal architecture, automated tests and a contribution to the CI/CD pipeline.

projects.name: NesGen
projects.description: An experiment in teaching a model to compose NES-style music, the sound of old-school video games. I explored Transformer and GAN approaches on the NES-MDB dataset, with MIDI tokenization and fine-tuning.

projects.name: Scooby
projects.description: A web crawler and scraper written in Scala 3, with an internal DSL to describe navigation, extraction and export. Concurrent execution is handled with Akka Typed.
